title: What Should You Do After Losing a Ball in a Red Penalty Area?
question: If your ball goes into a red penalty area and you can't retrieve it, which relief options are allowed under the Rules (each for one penalty stroke)? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Replay your shot from the previous spot.
Drop a ball within two club-lengths of the point where it crossed into the penalty area.
Drop a ball anywhere you like on the course, with no penalty.
Drop a ball behind the penalty area, keeping the entry point between you and the hole.

explanation: If your ball is lost in a red penalty area, you may: replay the shot, drop within two club-lengths of the entry point, or drop behind the penalty area on a straight line from the hole—each for one penalty stroke.

juniorVersion.title: What Can You Do If You Lose Your Ball in a Red Penalty Area?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball goes into a red penalty area, like a pond marked with red stakes, and you can't get it back. What are you allowed to do for one penalty shot? Pick all the answers that are correct.

choices.text: Hit another ball from the same place you last played.
Drop a ball within two club-lengths from where your ball went into the red area.
Drop a ball anywhere on the course with no penalty.
Drop a ball farther away from the hole, in line with where your ball entered the red area.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball is lost in a red penalty area, you can: hit again from your last spot, drop nearby (within two club-lengths), or drop behind the red area, keeping where your ball went in between you and the hole. Each way costs one penalty shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A part of the golf course, like a pond or stream, marked by red or yellow lines or stakes.
The length of your golf club. It's used to measure where you can drop your ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Walk the children to a real penalty area, show red stakes, and act out the drop choices with them. Use clubs to measure two club-lengths together.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can drop the ball anywhere you want without a penalty.
Not knowing what a penalty area looks like or where a ball entered it.
Forgetting you get only two club-lengths to drop beside the entry spot.
